result:
Fixed.

**Root cause:** `UnixListener::bind` and `UnixStream::connect` detect an abstract address by checking for a leading `\0`, then pass the *entire* byte string — NUL included — to `std::os::linux::net::SocketAddrExt::from_abstract_name`. But that constructor writes the leading NUL into `sun_path` itself; it expects just the name. So binding `"\0aaa"` registered the abstract name `"\0aaa"` (`sun_path` = `\0\0aaa`), and `as_abstract_name()` on the resulting address returned `b"\0aaa"` instead of `b"aaa"`.

Bind and connect were wrong in the same way, so they still found each other — which is why the existing test passed and the mismatch only showed up once the test inspected the registered address.

**Fix** (`tokio/src/net/unix/listener.rs:83`, `tokio/src/net/unix/stream.rs:79`): use `strip_prefix(b"\0")` instead of `starts_with`, passing only the name after the NUL.

**Verification:**
- `abstract_socket_name` in `uds_stream.rs` now passes; all 8 tests in that suite pass.
- `uds_datagram` (12), `uds_socket` (3), and `uds_split` (1) all pass — no regression in the ordinary pathname case.

I also checked the third potential call site, `UnixSocket::bind`/`connect` in `tokio/src/net/unix/socket.rs`, which goes through `socket2::SockAddr::unix` instead. That routine copies the bytes into `sun_path` verbatim and special-cases a leading NUL for the length calculation, so it already handles abstract names correctly and needed no change.
